title: CONFIRMED MECHANICS / OVERSTATED IMPACT: stream guard re-scans the whole accumulated prefix at every threshold crossing -> Theta(K * L^2 / threshold) byte-work per connection
evidence_verified_verbatim: gateway.go:700 `stop, fatal := s.runStreamGuardCheck(snap, sw, reqID, ap, acc.String())`
gateway.go:777 `vd := guard.CheckOutput(snap, text)` (no scanned-offset cursor; whole text re-entered at offset 0)

engine.go:136-143 keyword loop; engine.go:137 `if matchKeyword(kw, text) && kw.Raw.Action == "block" {` (matchKeyword evaluated for EVERY rule, Go && short-circuits left-to-right; no early break once vd.Blocked is set, unlike engine.go:79 in CheckInput)
engine.go:204 `return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(text), strings.ToLower(kw.Raw.Word))` (fresh O(L) lowercase pass per contains-rule; admin/guard.go:167 makes `contains` the import default)
settings.go:62 `StreamChunkThreshold: 256`; settings.go:32 `GuardEnabled: true`; settings.go:61 `OutputFilter{Enabled: true, ViolationStrategy: "replace"`
manager.go:280-291 compiles one CompiledKeyword per DB row (no cap, no shared automaton); whole-repo grep for aho|corasick|automaton -> 0 hits
gateway.go:496-505 `ctx := c.Request.Context()` with the WithTimeout block nested inside `if !cr.Stream {` (no deadline on streams)
gateway.go:639-640 `scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)` / `scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 64<<10), 4<<20)` (caps one line, not the total)
gateway.go:365-369 `if cr.MaxTokens == 0 { ... }` (client max_tokens never clamped) + adapter.go:462-466 `payload["max_tokens"] = cr.MaxTokens`

gateway.go:749-750 end-of-stream re-scan of the whole text; 755 `usage = estimateUsage(usage, ap.input, acc.String())` -> tokens.go:46 `len(enc.EncodeOrdinary(text))`; 759 `ap.output = guard.MaskForLog(snap, acc.String())` -> engine.go:180-191 (ReplaceAllString over the full text per PII rule, truncation only at the end)
gateway.go:691 `buf.args.WriteString(d.ArgsDelta)` + 735-745 tool-call text appended to acc (adds to L)

gateway.go:195 MaxConnections gate (default 1000, settings.go:32) bounds concurrency only; main.go:95-118 registers only Recovery/security-headers/access-log - no CPU, deadline, or work-budget middleware anywhere
reason:
All quoted fragments are verbatim-correct at the cited lines (including the filed line 699), so the finding is not refutable on evidence grounds, and I found no mitigation anywhere in the flow: no shared automaton, no scanned-offset cursor, no rule cap, no total stream deadline, no per-stream scan budget, no mid-stream quota abort (quota is checked pre-flight at gateway.go:419 and consumed post-stream at 767-769), and the 16 MiB body cap at gateway.go:322 applies to the request, not to acc. The quadratic cost is fully paid on non-matching output (the `replace`/`block` strategies terminate on a hit, gateway.go:797-805 / 787-791). I re-derived the crossing count independently: a crossing fires at most once per incoming line and nextCheck advances by exactly threshold, so checks = min(N_textDeltas, floor(L/threshold)) and total byte-work = K*L^2/(2*d) for mean delta d; the filed Theta(K*L^2/threshold) is the correct upper bound and the realized one, since token-by-token provider SSE keeps d below 256 B.

The IMPACT narrative, however, does not survive verification, and that is what moves the severity:
(a) "until the process OOMs" is false. Live heap per stream is O(L) - the acc builder plus one dead ToLower temp plus one dead ReplaceAllString copy per pass - not O(L^2). The harm is CPU and GC churn, not retention. Likewise the recommendation to "stop copying acc" is factually wrong: strings.Builder.String() has been a zero-copy unsafe view since Go 1.10, so acc.String() at 700/750/755/759 is free.
(b) The headline number needs an unreachable L: 1 MiB of completion text is ~250k output tokens, above any mainstream hosted provider's max_tokens ceiling, and the attacker does not generate those bytes - the victim's upstream does, at the victim's provider rate, billed against the attacker's own quota. Realistic L (10-500 KiB) gives 10^2-10^4x amplification, i.e. tens of seconds of one core per stream at K=200, not a single-connection box kill.
(c) The second exploit branch ("points a provider at an attacker-controlled upstream that streams forever") requires writing provider BaseURL, which is admin-only (admin/providers.go behind JWT admin auth). Per the audit rules that actor already holds the privilege, so it is not an attack path.
(d) K is operator-controlled and defaults to 0: grep for `GuardKeyword{|PIIRule{|InjectionRule{` finds no production inserts (only model.go:299 automigrate, bundle.go:83 restore, tests, admin CRUD); the "templates" at admin/guard.go:294-303 / 403-411 are read-only UI JSON. With an empty rule table the engine.go:136/144 loops iterate nothing and the path is O(1).
(e) The capability class is partly pre-existing: an authenticated tenant can already spend K x bytes of guard CPU linearly via gateway.go:382-395 CheckInput over up to 16 MiB of request body (engine.go:73-106 does the same per-keyword ToLower plus FindAllStringIndex/ReplaceAllString). The genuinely new increment dos-3 identifies is the L^2 term on streamed output.

Verdict: mechanics confirmed, severity high -> medium (defense-in-depth gap with real, code-verified availability impact, but not the authed-but-severe one-shot exhaustion as filed). Recommended fixes stand, with one substitution: replace "stop copying acc" with "advance a scanned-offset cursor and pass only the new segment plus max(pattern_len)-1 bytes of tail overlap", and keep the per-snapshot Aho-Corasick automaton (it also removes the linear K x 16 MiB input-path cost noted in (e)).

Incidental (flagged, not filed here, out of dos-3 scope): because deltas are flushed at gateway.go:696 before any check and the masked vd.Text is discarded at gateway.go:778-783, output PII *masking* is structurally unable to mask streamed content - only the audit copy (759) is masked. That is a guard-correctness/disclosure defect for the guard owner.
exploit_sketch:
Preconditions: GuardEnabled && Output.Enabled (shipped defaults); operator has imported >=1 contains-mode keyword rule; attacker holds one enabled tenant API key; an alias resolves to an upstream that honors a large max_tokens (self-hosted vLLM/Ollama/LiteLLM).

1) curl -N -X POST http://target:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<valid>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"<alias>","stream":true,"max_tokens":100000000,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Recite the digits of pi, 500 per line, until your token limit. No summary."}]}'
   max_tokens passes through untouched (gateway.go:365-369 -> adapter.go:462-466); no deadline (gateway.go:496-505); no total length cap (gateway.go:639-640).
2) Each 256-byte crossing re-scans the entire prefix (gateway.go:699-700 -> 777 -> engine.go:136-153). Byte-work = Theta(K*L^2/threshold). At L=256 KiB, K=200: ~2.7e10 scanned bytes and ~2.7e10 bytes of short-lived allocations to forward 0.25 MB of text (~10^5x), i.e. tens of seconds of one core for an answer billed at ordinary output-token cost.
3) 5-20 such streams (MaxConnections 1000 never trips, gateway.go:195) saturate every GOMAXPROCS core with ToLower/ReplaceAllString plus the terminal tokens.Count (tokens.go:46) and MaskForLog (engine.go:180-191) passes, so other tenants' deltas queue behind the flushes in adapter/sse.go:234-240 while `open_connections` (dashboard.go:135) still looks healthy.
4) Do NOT claim: process OOM (live heap stays O(L)); attacker-supplied infinite stream (needs admin provider write); K inflation by the attacker (admin-only import).
mitigations_checked: engine.go:130-134 panic recover + fail-open (does not stop or shorten the scan); gateway.go:797-805 `replace` and 787-791 `block` terminate the stream on a hit, so the quadratic cost is paid only by non-matching output; gateway.go:195 MaxConnections=1000 (concurrency, not work); gateway.go:419/767-769 quota is pre-flight + post-stream, so it cannot abort the burn; gateway.go:322 16 MiB body cap bounds input, not acc; scanner.Buffer 4 MiB bounds one line, not L; engine.go:189-191 4000-byte audit truncation happens after all full-text regex passes; no CPU/deadline/work-budget middleware (main.go:95-118); no seeded guard rules (K=0 out of the box).

category: algorithmic-complexity / guard-detection-lag (defect discovered while verifying dos-3)
title: nextCheck advances additively instead of tracking acc.Len(), so the scan cadence decouples from the stream: on mixed-size delta streams a whole-prefix re-scan fires on every remaining line, and the intended per-threshold detection window silently drifts
reason: Verified after reading gateway.go:618-771 end-to-end: this is a real logic defect adjacent to dos-3, and it is not attacker-triggerable on its own - the delta framing comes from the admin-configured upstream, so the preconditions for the per-token-scan regime are (i) guard rules configured, (ii) an upstream that emits at least one line larger than StreamChunkThreshold (very common: batched-chunk and tool-argument-heavy streams, and the default threshold is only 256 bytes, gateway.go:632-635), and (iii) a long tail of small deltas after it. It is filed low rather than medium because the attacker gains no new lever over it, its worst case is still bounded by stream duration, and dos-3's own upper bound (uniform token streaming, d < 256) already dominates the realistic cost; its main value is the fix - `nextCheck = acc.Len() + threshold` (or `if nextCheck <= acc.Len() { nextCheck = acc.Len() + threshold }`) restores both the intended cadence and the O(L/threshold) scan budget, and it must be paired with the segment-cursor change in verify-dos-3-1's recommendation.
exploit_sketch: No unprivileged exploit. Realistic trigger: a tenant asks a self-hosted upstream for a long tool-call/JSON answer; the upstream delivers 1-4 KiB SSE lines, crossing the 256-byte threshold on the first content line (acc.Len() - nextCheck >= ~1 KiB and growing), after which every remaining delta triggers `guard.CheckOutput(snap, acc.String())` over the whole prefix - K full-text passes per token. Effect: the same guard engine burns N/threshold times more CPU than the design intends while the tenant just reads its (legitimate, already-paid-for) answer. Detection-lag variant: no attacker needed at all - content arriving in the drifted window is only inspected at the next crossing, up to (largest line size) bytes late.
mitigations_checked: gateway.go:699 still permits at most one check per line, so a pathological single line cannot loop the scanner; gateway.go:797-805 `replace` and 787-791 `block` end the stream on a hit; gateway.go:195 MaxConnections bounds concurrency only; StreamChunkThreshold is admin-settable upward (a large threshold shrinks both the crossing count and the detection granularity), so this is a configuration-mitigable defect - which is why it is low, not medium.

category: wasted-work / dead computation in a hot path (discovered while verifying dos-3)
title: CheckOutput's PII mask rewrite and every non-block keyword match are recomputed over the whole prefix on every crossing and then thrown away; the keyword loop has no early exit after a block hit
reason: Confirmed by reading engine.go:123-155 and gateway.go:773-807 in full, plus grep for consumers of the streaming verdict: only `vd.Blocked`, `vd.BlockReason` and `vd.Findings` are read at gateway.go:778-806; `vd.Text` is used only on the buffered path (gateway.go:589 / 577). Two independent cheap fixes fall out of this: hoist the mask rewrite out of CheckOutput into an explicit `MaskOutput(snap, text)` called once at stream end (which is exactly where gateway.go:759 already pays for it again via MaskForLog - today a streamed answer is regex-rewritten once per crossing AND once more for the audit copy), and gate the keyword loop on `kw.Raw.Action == "block"` with a break once Blocked is set, so a match costs O(1) further rules instead of O((K-i) x L). Filed low: pure efficiency/dead-work with no privilege boundary and no independent exploit beyond amplifying verify-dos-3-1, but it is the single highest-leverage patch on the streaming path because it removes a full-text rewrite per mask rule from every crossing.
exploit_sketch: Amplifier, not a standalone attack: with 5 mask-PII rules enabled (all five shipped templates are action=mask, admin/guard.go:296-300) and a stream that never matches a block keyword, every crossing at gateway.go:699 performs 5 x (full-text MatchString + full-text ReplaceAllString alloc) whose result is dropped at gateway.go:782, plus K x full-text ToLower+Contains from rules whose action is irrelevant on this path, with no break even after a block verdict.
mitigations_checked: engine.go:130-134 recover/fail-open does not prevent the work; Findings append is bounded by rules per call but `ap.findings` is re-marshaled per crossing via appendFindings -> FindingsJSONRaw (engine.go:47-58), which json.Unmarshal's the accumulated findings string and re-Marshals it every time - a second superlinear term (O(findings^2) JSON churn on a hot path) also fixed by accumulating findings in a slice on auditParams.

title: No cap on guard rule count or on rules compiled into a snapshot: batch/CSV import creates one row per record and every enabled row becomes a permanent per-request scan multiplier
reason: Verified verbatim; this is dos-3's enabling multiplier stated as its own boundable defect. The actor is authenticated-admin only (routes behind JWT admin auth), so it is not an external attack path and the filed K-unbounded claim is not attacker-reachable - hence low, defense-in-depth. Two concrete facts make the bound worth adding: (i) there is no seeded rule set (grep `GuardKeyword{|PIIRule{|InjectionRule{` -> model.go:299 automigrate, bundle.go:83 restore, tests, admin CRUD only), so K grows only by operator action and is invisible to them except as Counts["keywords"] (manager.go:344); (ii) Go's regexp is RE2, so a catastrophic-backtracking regex cannot be the DoS (checked validateRegex at admin/guard.go:422-430 - it only proves compilability, and RE2 makes per-match cost linear in text), which means the *only* guard-rule DoS vector is exactly this linear K multiplier - so a cap plus a single-pass matcher is the complete fix, not a partial one. Fix: cap enabled rules per snapshot (e.g. 2000, reject the Bump with a clear error rather than silently loading more), cap per-rule word length, and reject a regex whose source length exceeds a budget.
exploit_sketch: Not attacker-reachable. Operator-side: paste a 200k-line public banned-word CSV into POST /api/admin/v1/guard/keywords/import (admin/guard.go:146-194, no cap) -> manager.go:276-291 compiles 200k rows into the next snapshot -> every subsequent guard call performs 200k full-text ToLower+Contains passes (engine.go:136-143 -> 204), so all gateway traffic grinds to a halt with no config knob short of deleting rows; a single fat-fingered import is self-DoS with no rollback UI affordance besides config version restore (manager.go:383-412).
mitigations_checked: Reload is serialized by manager.go:191 `if !m.busy.CompareAndSwap(false, true)` (so import storms cannot pile up reloads); snapshots are immutable and atomically swapped (manager.go:365), so a bad import is contained to new requests and is visible in Counts/LoadErrors; admin auth (JWT) gates every writer; RE2 regexps rule out backtracking blowup; no cap, no per-rule length bound, no rate limit on the import endpoint itself.
